rationale: The candidate reads as a compact, coherent mass in each individual view, so repair integrity is fairly strong, but the overall form is still too generic and slightly over-abstracted for neighborhood living. The dominant geometry is a single bent/angled block with a notch, yet the visible plan and elevations do not convincingly establish one clear occupiable ground relation or a robust public threshold at the verified access edge. The blue frontage edge is answered only weakly: there is no strongly legible court, undercut, entry seam, or ground-level opening that feels aligned to access. The courtyard idea exists in the genotype but is not visibly persuasive enough in the rendered mass, and the upper form reads more like a sculptural wedge than a capacity-aware mixed-use street building. The silhouette is coherent but not exceptional as a programmatic section; it is closer to an expressive object than an active neighborhood building. Because the program brief requires an active ground edge and public void/terrace logic, the visible mass does not yet hard-pass program fit.
